organization: Munk School of Global Affairs & Public Policy / Foreign Policy
notes: One of the world's richest nonfiction prizes (CA$50,000), awarded for the best English-language nonfiction book on international affairs. name: Duff Cooper Prize

name: FT Business Book of the Year
notes: Annual prize for the best business book of the year, backed by the Financial Times. Sponsor has changed: Goldman Sachs (2005–2013), McKinsey (2014–2021), Schroders (2023–present). Prize is £30,000. One of the most internationally recognized nonfiction awards, covering economics, business, politics, and social science.

categories.name: Business Book of the Year
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Financial Times Business Book of the Year Award
categories.coverageNotes: Winners and shortlists from 2005 onward. Wikipedia article uses prose bullet lists (not a wikitable); winners marked with {{blue ribbon}} template.

name: Robert F. Kennedy Book Award
organization: Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center
notes: Founded in 1980 to recognize books that reflect Robert F. Kennedy's concern for justice, opportunity, and the rights of poor and powerless people. The official laureate archive begins with the 1981 award. The program is not formally restricted to nonfiction; this nonfiction corpus excludes its 1988 fiction winner, Beloved.

categories.name: Book Award
categories.sourceLabel: Robert F. Kennedy Human Rights official book laureate archive and laureate pages
categories.coverageNotes: Official laureate records from 1981 through 2025. Multiple works described by official detail pages as receiving the award are normalized as co-winners. March: Book One (2014) is retained as an honorable mention because the historical winners list calls it a special recognition; The Burning Season (1991) is likewise marked honorable mention from a contemporary report. Beloved (1988) is excluded as fiction. The archive repeats the 1995 heading for Jack Bass, whose official detail page and contemporary records identify his award as 1994; the importer corrects that isolated heading error. Historical finalist slates were not published and are not inferred.

name: Francis Parkman Prize
notes: Annual prize for a nonfiction work of history on an American theme, judged for both literary merit and historical contribution.

categories.name: Francis Parkman Prize
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: Francis Parkman Prize winners
categories.coverageNotes: Winners from 1957 onward; no prize was awarded in 1968. Historical rows use the deterministic secondary list because the official archive is protected from automated retrieval. The 2026 winner is replaced with the Society of American Historians' official announcement. Special-achievement awards to people or publishers are excluded.

name: John Burroughs Medal
notes: Long-running medal for distinguished natural-history writing, first awarded in 1926. The current official historical archive is unavailable to automated retrieval, so the importer preserves a deterministic secondary list and uses publisher evidence for the newest winner.

categories.name: John Burroughs Medal
categories.sourceLabel: Wikipedia: John Burroughs Medal recipients
categories.coverageNotes: Book winners from 1926 through 2025, excluding explicit no-award years and three out-of-scope works: the poetry collection Nature Poems (1928) and the two fiction winners, Those of the Forest (1955) and Martin Marten (2017). The source has no 2019 entry, which remains an explicit unresolved gap rather than being labeled a no-award year. The 2018 lifetime-achievement medal for nature poetry is not a book record and is excluded.
